Does anyone see what I might be doing incorrectly from the call...?

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Why the Warning to run part 4 before any other???
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Why the Warning to run part 4 before any other???
messages.body_plain:
Your call to function g.shell.GGIR includes the argument "do.report=c(2,4)" this means that you instruct it to also generate a report for part 4.

If you only run part 1 or 1 and 2 then the warning informs you that expecting a part 4 report is not realistic, because you have not ran part 1-4 yet.

Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Why the Warning to run part 4 before any other???
messages.body_plain:
You can still process part 2 in parallel, just do not use "do.report=c(2)" when you do this because the report generation as invoked by 'do.report' would be done for each of those parallel sessions.
Once all milestone data for part 2 has been generated, you can run g.shell.GGIR again but this time with arguments mode=c() and do.report=c(2) to generate the summary report.

The same approach works for part 4 and part 5.
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

I am attempting to use the GGIR package for some of my data but am having trouble getting the outputs for the correct days and nights. I have tried a number of combinations of the different strategies, excludfirstlast and maxdur and days window. I can get the correct nights or correct days but not at the same time.

I am looking to get 6 days and 6 nights of data, in the study participants collected the accelerometers at various times throughout the day on a Monday, they then returned the accelerometer at the earliest on the next Monday. I have 50 participants and would like to look at the PA data for 6 days from waking on the Tuesday until sleeping on the Sunday, and 6 nights of sleep Tuesday through to Sunday. The only way I can see I can do it at the moment would be to use strategy 1 and alter hrs.del.start for each participant. messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robin,
GGIR can only remove X numbers at the beginning and end, or exclude the first and last day.  If you want specific nights to be included or excluded and if these do not occur on the same day of measurement for each participant then best approach is to focus on the day and night specific output, and clean the data yourself by removing the nights or days you are not interested in.
Next, you can calculate the person average yourself.
Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

This is a gentle reminder that if you think that GGIR is valuable for your research then please consider subscribing to my sustainability service: https://www.movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir.

Needless to say that reporting your issues on github <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues> or here in the google group is always appreciated, but the efforts needed to help you address them are voluntary.

If you are not able to subscribe to the service then consider: actively helping out other GGIR users with questions and issues, contributing to the development of GGIR yourself in person, or getting funding to pay for a scientific programmer to work on GGIR on your behalf.

If you cannot or do not want to commit to either of these options then please understand that I will ignore or at least put a lot less priority on your issues.

Thanks, Vincent

messages.subject_clean: date format with function g.inspectfile and g.getstarttime
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

Thank you so much for developing this very helpful package. I have been using it with Actigraph data and it is really helpful. In the process I found two bugs that may be easily fixed.

In g.inpectfile, line 138:
tmp3 = as.character(unlist(strsplit(tmp2, "yy.at <http://yy.at>."))[2])

It is limited by the format of the date (it has to be the format */*/yyyy). Instead, this may work:
tmp3 = as.character(unlist(strsplit(tmp2, ".at.",fixed = T))[2])

Then in g.getstarttime, line 119-126, the same problem occurs with different date format specification. If data formats other than */*/yyyy could be included, i.e. yyyy/mm/dd (the thousands of data files that I have are unfortunately in this format), that would be great.

Thank you again for your hard work!

Best,
XInyue

messages.subject_clean: Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal
messages.body_plain:
I have activity data recorded over multiple days. During a subset of days, say days 4 to 12, the actigraph was either not worn or malfunctioned resulting in very low magnitude ENMO (mean < 0.1 with random spikes = 0.4). We did not use a sleep diary. For all nights during the "bad" period, we get the exact same sleep/wake up detection periods displayed between approximately midnight to 8am night after night. Any idea what would be causing this problem? We will of course ignore these nights from our analyses, but are wondering why an exact pattern repeats itself.

Thanks for your help,

Phil
